rule.title: DNS Server Error Failed Loading the ServerLevelPluginDLL
rule.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

es.summary: El servicio DNS de Windows registró un evento relacionado con la carga de un DLL de plugin a nivel de servidor (ServerLevelPluginDll) definido en el registro. Puede indicar un intento de ejecutar código como SYSTEM a través del servicio DNS, normalmente en un controlador de dominio.
es.what_it_detects: Eventos 150, 770 o 771 del log DNS Server (proveedor Microsoft-Windows-DNS-Server-Service), que se generan cuando el servicio DNS intenta cargar el DLL indicado en HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\DNS\Parameters\ServerLevelPluginDll. El evento 150 indica un fallo al cargar o inicializar ese DLL.
es.why_it_matters: Un miembro de DnsAdmins puede configurar un DLL arbitrario (por ejemplo con dnscmd /config /serverlevelplugindll) que el servicio DNS carga como SYSTEM al reiniciarse. En un controlador de dominio esto equivale a comprometer el dominio. Corresponde a secuestro de carga de DLL (T1574.001) para escalar privilegios y lograr persistencia.
triage_steps: Revise el EventID y el mensaje: anote la ruta del DLL y el código de error. Una ruta UNC o un directorio temporal es muy sospechoso.
Consulte el valor ServerLevelPluginDll en el registro del servidor DNS y compárelo con la configuración aprobada; normalmente no existe.
Busque en el mismo host, +/- 15 minutos, la creación de procesos dnscmd.exe con CommandLine que contenga serverlevelplugindll y el usuario que lo ejecutó.
Busque eventos de modificación del registro (Sysmon 13 o 4657) sobre DNS\Parameters y reinicios del servicio DNS (7036, 7040).
Verifique si el usuario implicado pertenece a DnsAdmins y si hubo cambios recientes en ese grupo (eventos 4728, 4732, 4756).
Si el DLL existe, obtenga su hash, firma y fecha de creación; revise conexiones SMB salientes del servidor hacia la ruta indicada.
Revise procesos hijos de dns.exe y conexiones de red inusuales tras el reinicio del servicio, y alertas previas del mismo usuario u host.
false_positives: Instalación o actualización documentada de un plugin DNS legítimo (por ejemplo, soluciones de filtrado o seguridad DNS) que registra un DLL de servidor.
Restos de un plugin desinstalado cuyo valor de registro quedó apuntando a un DLL inexistente, generando el evento 150 en cada arranque.
Pruebas autorizadas de red team o pentest sobre controladores de dominio.
response_steps: Confirme con el equipo de infraestructura si existe un cambio aprobado para ese plugin; si no, trate el caso como incidente de alta prioridad.
Preserve evidencia: exporte el log DNS Server, la clave de registro y una copia del DLL con su hash antes de modificar nada.
Contenga: elimine el valor ServerLevelPluginDll tras validarlo, reinicie el servicio DNS en ventana controlada y aísle el host si hubo ejecución.
Restablezca credenciales de la cuenta usada, revise y depure la membresía de DnsAdmins y busque persistencias adicionales en el dominio.
Recupere y fortalezca: monitoree cambios en DNS\Parameters y el uso de dnscmd, y restrinja DnsAdmins a cuentas administrativas necesarias.
es.severity_rationale: El nivel alto es adecuado porque estos eventos son poco comunes en servidores DNS normales y señalan una técnica conocida para ejecutar código como SYSTEM en controladores de dominio.

en.summary: The Windows DNS service logged an event about loading a server-level plugin DLL (ServerLevelPluginDll) set in the registry. This can mean someone is trying to run code as SYSTEM through the DNS service, usually on a domain controller.
en.what_it_detects: DNS Server log events 150, 770 or 771 (provider Microsoft-Windows-DNS-Server-Service). The service writes them when it tries to load the DLL named in HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\DNS\Parameters\ServerLevelPluginDll. Event 150 means that DLL failed to load or initialize.
en.why_it_matters: A DnsAdmins member can register any DLL, for example with dnscmd /config /serverlevelplugindll. The DNS service then loads it as SYSTEM when it restarts. On a domain controller that gives control of the domain. This is DLL hijacking (T1574.001), used for privilege escalation and persistence.
triage_steps: Read the EventID and message. Record the DLL path and error code. A UNC path or a temp directory is highly suspicious.
Check the ServerLevelPluginDll registry value on the DNS server against the approved configuration. Normally the value does not exist.
On the same host, +/- 15 minutes, search for dnscmd.exe process creation with serverlevelplugindll in CommandLine, and note which user ran it.
Look for registry changes to DNS\Parameters (Sysmon 13 or 4657) and for DNS service restarts (7036, 7040).
Check whether that user is in DnsAdmins and whether the group's membership changed recently (4728, 4732, 4756).
If the DLL exists, collect its hash, signature and creation time. Check for outbound SMB from the server to the referenced path.
After the service restart, look for child processes of dns.exe, unusual network connections and earlier alerts for the same user or host.
false_positives: A documented install or update of a legitimate DNS plugin, such as a DNS filtering or security product, that registers a server-level DLL.
A leftover registry value from an uninstalled plugin that points to a missing DLL and triggers event 150 at every service start.
Authorized red team or penetration testing against domain controllers.
response_steps: Ask the infrastructure team whether an approved change covers this plugin. If none exists, handle it as a high-priority incident.
Preserve evidence before changing anything: export the DNS Server log and the registry key, and copy the DLL and record its hash.
Contain: once validated, remove the ServerLevelPluginDll value, restart DNS in a controlled window, and isolate the host if code ran.
Reset credentials for the account involved, clean up DnsAdmins membership and hunt for other persistence in the domain.
Recover and harden: monitor DNS\Parameters changes and dnscmd use, and limit DnsAdmins to the admin accounts that need it.
en.severity_rationale: High fits because these events are rare on normal DNS servers and point to a known way of running code as SYSTEM on domain controllers.

positive.description: Event 150: the DNS service on a domain controller failed to load a plugin DLL referenced from a remote UNC path.

event.Message: The DNS server could not load or initialize the plug-in DLL \\198.51.100.23\share\plugin.dll. The event data is the error code.

positive.description: Event 770 logged by the DNS service while it handled the ServerLevelPluginDll configured in the registry.

event.Message: DNS Server plugin DLL C:\Windows\Temp\dnsplug.dll event.

negative.description: Routine event 2 on the same DNS server: the service started normally, with no plugin DLL activity.
Event 4013 on the DNS server: it is waiting for the initial Active Directory synchronization. This is common at boot and has nothing to do with plugins.

event.Message: The DNS server is waiting for Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) to signal that the initial synchronization of the directory has been completed.
